item.title: Gulshan warehouse linked to Salman Muqtadir’s father-in-law sealed
item.description:
The Department of Narcotics Control (DNC) has sealed a bonded warehouse in Gulshan owned by the father-in-law of content creator Salman Muqtadir after identifying irregularities in the storage and accounting of imported liquor and beer.
The warehouse, TOS Bond Pvt Ltd, is owned by Nur Islam, his wife Sheila Islam and their daughter Tasnim Islam.
The DNC disclosed the information in a press release on Friday morning.
A joint team led by the DNC, along with the Customs Intelligence and Investigation Department and SRB, conducted the operation on Thursday night.
During the operation, officials checked the company's registers, National Board of Revenue-approved software and the physical stock at the warehouse.
They found 144 cans of beer, 12 bottles of whisky and six bottles of Nemiroff in the warehouse, although the company's software showed the products as "Exbond", meaning they had already been released from the warehouse.
The team also found that 2,250 cartons of imported Heineken beer were listed as "Inbound" in the company's software on September 3, 2026. However, the goods were not physically present at the warehouse.
Officials also found that the company had four floors, but the necessary customs authorisation and related documents for two floors were unavailable.
Following the findings, customs authorities sealed the warehouse in the presence of DNC officials under the relevant customs law.
The DNC said further verification is underway and legal action will be taken based on the findings.

item.title: Vegetable prices remain high in Dhaka markets
item.description:
Prices of essential commodities have yet to ease in Dhaka, with most vegetables selling at Tk80 or more per kg.
Although the winter vegetable season is approaching, its impact on the market has yet to be felt, leaving consumers paying higher prices for vegetables.
Egg prices have also increased in some areas, while chicken prices remain unchanged. Prices of some fish have also risen.
The information was gathered from visits to several markets in the capital on Friday.
Bitter gourd, arum stems, pointed gourd, spiny gourd and cucumber were selling for Tk80 per kg. Okra was Tk60, while bottle gourd was Tk60-80 depending on size.
Carrots were selling for Tk140 per kg, papaya Tk30, tomatoes Tk120, potatoes Tk30, onions Tk50, beans Tk200, yardlong beans Tk100 and round eggplant Tk140. Long eggplant was Tk100 per kg.
Beans were the most expensive vegetable at Tk200 per kg, followed by carrots and round eggplant at Tk140 and tomatoes at Tk120.
The price of green chillies, however, has fallen slightly. They were selling for Tk160-180 per kg, down from Tk200.
There was little relief in the fish market, with prices of some varieties increasing.
Rohu was selling for Tk400-600 per kg depending on size and quality, compared with Tk400-500 last week. Pabda was Tk600, koi Tk330, tilapia Tk230 and pangas Tk250-280 per kg.
Shrimp was selling for Tk1,500-2,500 per kg depending on size.
Pabda prices have increased from last week, when the fish sold for Tk450-500 per kg.
Broiler chicken was selling for Tk180 per kg, unchanged from last week, while cock chicken was Tk330 per kg.
Egg prices varied by location, with a dozen selling for Tk150-160.
Rahman Mia, a customer at a market, said: “Vegetable prices may seem lower individually, but buying several types at once costs quite a lot. Beans, chillies and carrots are particularly expensive. Fish and eggs are also not cheap.”
Another customer, Jibon Loskar Ray, said: “Every day, I have to worry about the price of one product or another. Buying all the essentials for the family costs more than the budget. We hope prices will fall somewhat when winter vegetables arrive.”
Traders said vegetable prices could fall further as supplies of winter vegetables increase.
They said prices of some products continue to change depending on demand and supply, transportation costs and overall market conditions.

item.title: Navy rescues 65 Malaysia-bound migrants, detains 11 traffickers
item.description:
The Bangladesh Navy has rescued 65 people from a wooden boat being used to transport people illegally to Malaysia by sea and detained 11 suspected human traffickers.
The rescue was carried out on Wednesday night during a routine patrol in the Saint Martin's area, according to a release issued by the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) on Friday morning.
BNS Khalid Bin Walid intercepted the boat after a fishing vessel, FV Crystal-1, spotted it drifting about 81 nautical miles from the Saint Martin's Lighthouse, the release said.
The fishing vessel approached the boat after noticing that its engine had failed. Its crew later informed the Navy after becoming suspicious of the people on board.
Navy personnel reached the scene and rescued all 76 people. As water was entering the wooden boat, they removed the water to prevent it from sinking and provided the people with first aid, food and other humanitarian assistance.
During preliminary interrogation, 11 of the 76 people were identified as members of a human trafficking ring and subsequently detained.
The remaining 65 were identified as victims who had been lured with promises of passage to Malaysia.
Most of the victims had allegedly been abducted by the trafficking ring and held captive in remote areas of Teknaf in Cox’s Bazar before being taken by sea towards Malaysia.
The detained suspects and the seized boat are being handed over to Teknaf Police Station for further legal action, the ISPR said.
The Bangladesh Navy continues regular patrols and operations to secure the country's maritime boundaries and prevent human trafficking, smuggling and other illegal activities at sea.

item.title: Ronaldo's Portugal future in doubt after walkout
item.description:
The international future of Portugal superstar Cristiano Ronaldo hung in the balance after the 41-year-old walked out on the squad after learning that he would not start the game against Denmark on Thursday.
Ronaldo announced late on Wednesday that he had left the team, shortly after a press conference in which coach Jorge Jesus confirmed the five-time Ballon d'Or winner would be left out of his starting line-up for a second consecutive Nations League game.
In his absence, Portugal turned on the style to beat Denmark 4-2.
The former Real Madrid forward had been due to train with his teammates at the Parken Stadium on the eve of the game, but walked out following the announcement by Jesus.
"Following the national team coach's press conference, and after having a conversation with the Portuguese Football Federation president, I decided to leave the national team's training camp," Ronaldo wrote on Instagram.
He had already spent the entirety of Sunday's 2-1 Nations League win in Norway on the bench, having captained the side in the 1-0 home victory over Wales last Thursday.
Ronaldo appeared to indicate that the reasons behind Jesus's decision ran deeper, and hinted at a departure from the national team he has graced for more than two decades.
"In due course, I will tell the truth to all the Portuguese people about my reasons for leaving the national team, to which I have always been dedicated," Ronaldo said.
"Now is time to wish good luck to Portugal and to all my team-mates, without exception."
Spanish sports daily Marca said that Jesus and Portuguese federation president Pedro Proenca followed Ronaldo to Copenhagen airport in an attempt to persuade him to stay with the squad, before the player boarded his private jet.
Jesus insisted earlier on Wednesday that there was no rift between him and Ronaldo, although the 72-year-old, who was appointed in July, acknowledged that his captain was disappointed to remain on the bench against Norway.
The news sparked a wave of memes on social media and a furious backlash from Ronaldo's sister, Elma Aveiro.
"They don't deserve to have the best of anything," she said about the Portuguese people on Instagram.
"We are envious, scornful, and ignorant, and we deserve to return to the mediocrity that defined us in the pre-CR7 era of football," she added, using his nickname.
- 'Players with status' -
The game in Oslo was the first time since November 2024 that Ronaldo had not featured for Portugal while not being either injured or suspended.
"There was no incident whatsoever," Jesus, who coached Ronaldo at Saudi club Al-Nassr for a year, insisted after that match.
"Any player -- and I was a player myself... when you spend 20 or 30 minutes warming up and then don't get on... no one is happy about that," Jesus added on Wednesday.
The Portuguese coach also said that he had told Ronaldo before the match that he might bring him on as a substitute.
"Afterwards, as coach, I decided not to bring him on. It's nothing to make a fuss about," Jesus insisted.
After the win on Thursday, Jesus's press conference was dominated by talk of Ronaldo.
"This Portugal team scored four goals and put in a performance which, in my opinion, was of a very high standard," he said.
"Of course, this is more important than anything else that has happened.
"I still think exactly the same way: there are players with status. That much is crystal clear," he added.
"But I'll say it again: the rules are the same for everyone."
There were reports that Portuguese Prime Minister Luis Montenegro had even discussed the issue of Ronaldo's involvement with the coach on Wednesday.
Jesus said earlier in the day that against Denmark he again intended to start AC Milan striker Goncalo Ramos, who scored the winner in Norway.
Regarding Ronaldo, he said: "If I need him, he'll come on. If I don't need him, he won't."
Ronaldo recently announced that this would "probably (be) my last year in football".
He is Portugal's leading goalscorer and most capped player, with 146 goals in 234 appearances.
The former Sporting, Manchester United, Real and Juventus striker made his international debut aged 18 in 2003 and played in the Euro 2004 final when Portugal lost to hosts Greece.
He reached the World Cup semi-finals in 2006 and captained his country to glory at Euro 2016.
Ronaldo and Portugal were eliminated by eventual winners Spain in the last 16 of this year's World Cup.

item.title: Ex-lawmaker Akhtaruzzaman sued over alleged airport assault, disorder
item.description:
A case has been filed against Major (retd) Akhtaruzzaman, a former lawmaker, on charges of obstructing government duties, creating disorder at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport and assaulting a security official.
Airport security officer Md Shahriar Alam Sajib filed the case with Airport Police Station on Friday under several sections of the Code of Criminal Procedure, an official said.
According to the First Information Report (FIR), the incident took place around 10:40am on Thursday after passengers of a Biman Bangladesh Airlines flight (BG-338) arriving from Madina faced a shortage of trolleys and delays in collecting their baggage at No 8 baggage belt amid heavy passenger pressure.
As frustration and tension among the passengers escalated, Airport Executive Director Group Captain SM Ragib Samad went to the spot to bring the situation under control following a request from Dhaka-5 MP Mohammad Kamal Hossain.
The FIR said that while Ragib Samad was trying to calm the situation, Akhtaruzzaman, who was expelled from BNP several times and joined Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami in December 2025, allegedly moved towards him aggressively, abused him and threatened to beat him and throw him out of the airport by the neck.
He also allegedly made offensive remarks about the civil aviation and tourism minister.
The situation worsened when protocol assistants accompanying Akhtaruzzaman started recording videos on mobile phones in the airport's restricted Key Point Installation (KPI) area.
When security supervisor Warrant Officer Mohammad Kamal Uddin asked them to stop recording, Akhtaruzzaman allegedly abused him and physically assaulted him.
The FIR further alleged that Akhtaruzzaman threw bottles of holy Zamzam water collected by other passengers from their trolleys, allegedly causing damage, and behaved aggressively towards a representative of Biman Bangladesh Airlines.
Police said they will collect CCTV footage, statements from eyewitnesses and other evidence as part of the investigation and take legal action based on the findings.

item.title: Pharmacist injured in attack by expelled Jubo Dal leader in Banglamotor
item.description:
A pharmacist was injured after an expelled Jubo Dal leader allegedly attacked him with a pistol in Banglamotor, Dhaka, on Thursday night.
The injured man, Md Sohan, 35, received treatment at Dhaka Medical College Hospital.
Police detained four people in connection with the incident, including expelled Jubo Dal leader Ferdous Ahmed Saimon.
Sohan said Ferdous and several associates blocked his way in an alley north of Rupayan Tower in Banglamotor around Thursday night.
During an argument, Ferdous allegedly hit Sohan on the head with the butt of a pistol, leaving him bleeding.
Ferdous then allegedly fired two blank shots to create panic, Sohan said.
Hearing the gunshots, local residents came forward, prompting Ferdous and his associates to enter a nearby building. Residents gathered outside the building and protested the incident.
A video of the protest has circulated on social media. In the video, locals allege that Ferdous has long been extorting money in the area and attacking people who refuse to pay.
Tejgaon Division Deputy Commissioner Md Ibne Mizan said Ferdous Ahmed and two of his associates were detained and taken to Tejgaon Industrial Area police station around midnight.
Police said Sohan was beaten and struck on the head during an argument. Locals then surrounded Saimon and his associates.
Police went to the scene after being informed and brought the situation under control. Additional police were later deployed, and the situation returned to normal during the night.

item.title: James: A rockstar’s journey through time and tune
item.description:
As the sun sets on October 2, a remarkable milestone graces the life of a musical legend, a rockstar who has strummed the strings of our hearts for over four decades.
Faruq Mahfuz Anam James, affectionately known as Guru, is not merely a name but an indelible mark on the canvas of Bangladeshi music. His journey, like the melodies he crafts, is a symphony of passion, resilience, and artistic brilliance.
James, the lead guitarist and vocalist of the band Nagar Baul, formerly known as Feelings, has been the embodiment of music itself.
His journey began in the early 1980s, as he, alongside Funty, Pablo, and Swapan, breathed new life into Feelings when former members departed. Together, they ignited the local gig scene with their electric performances.
In those early days, James was hailed as “the one who can play mark knopfler with right feels.”
It wasn’t long before they ventured to Dhaka to record their debut album, “Station Road.” Although it didn’t attain immediate stardom, tracks like “Ager Jonome,” “Amai Zete Dao,” and “Rupshagor” became anthems in their own right.
It was in 1989 that James and Feelings released the game-changing album “Jail Theke Bolchhi” (words from a condemn cell). This masterpiece propelled Feelings into the mainstream alongside other giants like Souls, Feedback, and Chime.
James’s music transcends genres, from psychedelic rock to blues, and he has collaborated with an array of lyrical maestros, including Poet Shamsur Rahman, Prince Mahmud, Marjuk Rasel, Shibli, Anando and Deholovi. His melodies have been composed by luminaries like Lucky Akhand and Manam Ahmed.
In the tapestry of his musical influences, names like Jim Morrison, Mark Knopfler, and Eric Clapton shine brightly.
His discography reads like a chronicle of Bangladeshi rock, with albums like “Station Road,” “Jail theke Bolchi,” “Nogor Baul,” “Leis Fita Leis,” and “Collection of Feelings” etching their places in the annals of music history.
As the years rolled on, James embarked on a solo journey, delivering albums like “Annonna,” “Palabe Kothai,” “Dukkhini Dukkho Korona,” “Thik Achhe Bondhu,” “Ami Tomader E Lok,” “Jonota Express,” “Toofan,” and “Kal Jomuna.” He also transitioned Feelings into “Nagar Baul,” unleashing “Dushtu Cheler Dol” in 2001.
James”s magnetic aura extended beyond Bangladesh’s borders, resonating in the hearts of West Bengal’s music enthusiasts.
His rendezvous with Bollywood, starting with “Gangster” in 2005 and continuing with hits like “Bheegi Bheegi,” “Chal Chalein,” “Rishtey,” and “Alvida (Reprise),” amplified his global resonance.
In 2013, James lent his soul-stirring voice to the Hindi song “Bebasi” for the movie “Warning,” a gem cherished by his ever-growing fanbase.
Yet, even as the world celebrated his music, James remained a humble soul. His simplicity, devotion to his craft, and love for photography, especially his aspiration to capture the essence of poet Nirmalendu Goon through his lens, reveal the grounded artist behind the rockstar facade.
Recently, James surprised the world with two of his comeback singles, “I Love You” and “Shobi Bhul” after a hiatus of twelve years.
In a heartfelt statement, he expressed his gratitude to his loyal fans, promising the song, “I Love You” that resonates with his decades-long journey.
The burning question, “Why the hiatus?” remains unanswered, but as James put it, “It just happened.”
The music, like his heart, beckoned him back, and for that, his fans are eternally grateful.
James, often credited as a pioneer of “band music” in Bangladesh, is not just an artist but a testament to the ever-evolving spirit of Bangladeshi music.
He reminds us of the glorious past when albums were treasures, released in cassettes with captivating covers and posters, a stark contrast to today’s digital age.
Speaking of the “good old days,” James wistfully reminisced, “We lived through a great time; it’s sad that everything is presently digital.”
He hinted at the possibility of his new song being released in a physical format, rekindling nostalgia.
Beyond music, James’s photography has earned accolades on social media. While he cherishes it as a hobby for now, fans eagerly await the day he may decide to exhibit his captivating works.
James’s fame transcends boundaries, not only within Bangladesh but also in Bollywood, where his songs like “Bheegi Bheegi” and “Alvida” continue to mesmerize audiences across the subcontinent.
In a world that often transforms artists into legends, James remains the embodiment of simplicity, humility, and timeless music.
As he concluded his every concert with a simple “Love you all,” it echoed the love and admiration that millions hold for this musical guru.
On his 59th birthday, we salute James, the rockstar who not only graced our lives with music but also carved his place in our hearts, leaving an indelible mark for generations to come.
Happy Birthday, Guru, may your melodies continue to serenade our souls for years to come.

item.title: Shakib Khan’s ‘Mohabbat’ set for Eid-ul-Azha 2027

item.title: Trump vows to hit Iran 'very hard' if linked to flydubai attack
item.description:
US President Donald Trump warned on Thursday that Iran will be "hit very hard" if it is found to be linked to a pilot's attack on a flydubai flight to Israel.
The dramatic events a day earlier saw passengers help stop the plane from crashing, making an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia before the flight's mostly Israeli passengers were flown home to a hero's welcome.
Trump's warning came as the United Arab Emirates opened an investigation into whether the incident was linked to terrorism and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the suspect had undergone "Islamist radical indoctrination".
"I would say the answer, based on what I'm hearing, is yes but we're working on it right now," Trump told reporters Thursday when asked at the White House whether Iran was involved in what happened on the flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv.
On whether the United States would retaliate against Iran if it was found responsible, Trump replied: "Oh, they'll be hit very hard, don't worry."
Trump's threat coincided with a wider US military buildup in the region.
Axios reported that Washington had recently deployed additional Patriot missile batteries to Saudi Arabia and Qatar to help protect key energy facilities from possible Iranian retaliation.
The US news outlet also reported that the USS Theodore Roosevelt aircraft carrier and its strike group were heading to the Middle East, where they could join two other US carrier strike groups already in the region.
As speculation swirled about a possible motive, the UAE and Saudi Arabia began to piece together the events in the cabin.
Saudi Arabia said the co-pilot was transferred to the UAE on Thursday accompanied by an "Emirati security team", adding that its initial investigation showed he had attacked the aircraft's captain.
The alleged assault triggered a struggle for control of the aircraft before an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia. Passengers were later flown to Israel on a replacement flight.
"We know that he underwent Islamist radical indoctrination," Netanyahu told the "Fox & Friends" TV show, without elaborating.
"The attacker, he calls out to the aircrew, 'Kill me, kill me'," Netanyahu said, adding it was "clear he was suicidal".
His comments came after the UAE chief prosecutor said investigators would explore whether there had been "terrorist activity or intent".
Netanyahu said the UAE would lead the investigation while Israel would participate.
He identified the co-pilot as an Omani national and said Israel would check how he had been cleared to work on flights to the country.
"We have constraints that say that you can't have pilots from countries that don't have diplomatic relations with Israel. Obviously he was able to go through that," Netanyahu told Fox News.
Netanyahu had earlier credited captain Smit Machchhar, an Indian national, and passengers with averting catastrophe after the co-pilot allegedly stabbed him and tried to crash the plane.
Passengers described rushing the cockpit and a fight for control after the plane suddenly plummeted, losing around 17,000 feet of altitude in the span of a minute, according to the Flightradar24 website.
Israeli officials have called the incident "an attempted terrorist attack", although Netanyahu in an earlier interview with CBS News had not ruled out the possibility that mental health was to blame.
"During the flight, as they approached the country, one of the pilots stabbed the other pilot, and apparently tried to crash the plane with everyone on board," Netanyahu had said in a video message.
Netanyahu later praised Machchhar "for his extraordinary bravery".
The Indian ambassador to the UAE visited the wounded captain, with the embassy saying he was in "good health and recovering well".
Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi described him as a "HERO", saying his actions had helped save lives.
Passenger Miryam Shira Ohayon said the aircraft was "pretty much out of control" as the incident unfolded over Jordan.
"The co-pilot tried to murder the pilot and basically carry out a suicide attack on the plane," she told reporters.
"It was really on the way to crashing, and it was simply the resourcefulness of many people who took control of the co-pilot and neutralised him."
Flydubai said another "on-duty flydubai crew traveling on the flight... landed the aircraft safely" and announced it was suspending flights to Israel while the investigation continued.
Israeli President Isaac Herzog said he would honour five Israelis who helped overpower the co-pilot and prevent the plane from crashing.

item.title: AQI: Dhaka ranks 5th among world’s most polluted cities
item.description:
Dhaka ranked fifth among the world's most polluted cities on Friday morning, with an Air Quality Index (AQI) score of 163 recorded at 9:25am.
The air quality was classified as ‘unhealthy’, indicating that the level of air pollution may pose health risks to the general population, according to the AQI scale.
Pakistan's Lahore topped the list with an AQI score of 236.
Bahrain's Manama and India's Kolkata ranked second and third, respectively, with AQI scores of 176 each.
According to AQI standards, a reading between 101 and 150 is considered 'unhealthy for sensitive groups', while 151 to 200 is classified as 'unhealthy'. A reading between 201 and 300 is considered 'very unhealthy', while levels above 301 are deemed 'hazardous', posing serious health risks.
The AQI provides daily updates on air quality, indicating how clean or polluted the air is and highlighting potential health impacts.
In Bangladesh, the AQI is calculated based on five major pollutants: particulate matter (PM10 and PM2.5), nitrogen dioxide (NO2), carbon monoxide (CO), sulfur dioxide (SO2) and ozone.
Dhaka has long struggled with air pollution, with air quality typically deteriorating during winter and improving during the monsoon season.
The World Health Organization estimates that air pollution causes around seven million deaths globally each year, mainly from stroke, heart disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, lung cancer and acute respiratory infections.

item.title: Messi finalises acquisition of second Spanish lower league club
item.description:
Argentina icon Lionel Messi has officially acquired Eldense, a Spanish second-division club announced Thursday.
Eldense, based just in-land from Alicante, have become the former Barcelona attacker's second venture into Spanish football ownership after his purchase of Cornella, near Barcelona, in April.
"Club Deportivo Eldense officially announce (their) acquisition by Leo Messi," the club wrote in an online statement.
"Founded in 1921, CD Eldense embark on this new chapter with the ambition to consolidate their position and grow in professional football."
Messi, 39, has been playing for Inter Miami since 2023, where, according to media reports, his contract includes a provision for him to become a shareholder in the MLS club after he retires from the game.
The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner announced his retirement from international football in late August following the loss to Spain in the 2026 World Cup final.

item.title: Klopp earns first Germany win as Portugal progresses without Ronaldo
item.description:
Jürgen Klopp secured his first victory as Germany coach, while Portugal advanced with a convincing win over Denmark without veteran forward Cristiano Ronaldo in the Nations League on Thursday.
Florian Wirtz scored as Germany beat Serbia 2-0 in Munich, giving Klopp his first victory in his third match in charge and avoiding an unwanted record.
The 59-year-old had opened his tenure with a 1-1 draw against the Netherlands before Germany suffered a surprise 1-0 loss to Greece on Sunday.
Germany produced a disciplined and energetic performance against Serbia, reflecting the high-intensity style Klopp wants to establish.
“That's going in my archive. We'll make a video out of it now,” Klopp said. “That's how we want to play.”
Germany created several chances before Tom Bischof opened the scoring in the 39th minute, finishing the rebound after Wirtz's effort struck the post.
Klopp introduced Said El Mala after halftime for his Germany debut. Goalkeeper Jonas Urbig and Freiburg forward Derry Scherhant also made their international debuts.
Wirtz doubled Germany's lead after receiving Maximilian Mittelstädt's cross. He controlled the ball past a defender with his first touch before finding the inside of the right post with his second.
“It was important to win again, just for the spirit in the team, and to send a signal out that we're good football players and also a good football nation,” Wirtz said.
Netherlands held by Greece
Tijjani Reijnders scored in the 89th minute as the Netherlands came from behind to draw 2-2 with Greece in Thessaloniki in the other Group A2 match.
Fotis Ioannidis scored one goal and assisted on the other for Greece, while Virgil van Dijk scored before Reijnders rescued a point for the Netherlands.
The Dutch side had also needed a late equalizer in its previous match against Germany.
Greece remained top of Group A2 after recording away wins over Serbia and Germany.
Portugal wins without Ronaldo
Portugal defeated Denmark 4-2 in Copenhagen as João Félix sealed the victory late, with Ronaldo absent from the squad.
Ronaldo left the team a day earlier following an apparent dispute with coach Jorge Jesus, raising questions over his future with the national side.
Gonçalo Ramos, who replaced the 41-year-old forward, assisted João Cancelo for Portugal's opening goal before scoring the team's second two minutes after Mikkel Damsgaard equalized in the 23rd minute.
Rasmus Højlund leveled again in the 53rd, but Vitinha restored Portugal's advantage with a near-post header from Bruno Fernandes' free kick in the 67th.
Félix completed the scoring in the 87th minute.
Wales beats Norway
Wales defeated 10-man Norway 2-1 for its first Group A4 victory, with Erling Haaland failing to score.
Haaland failed to find the net for only the second time in his last 18 competitive international appearances. He has scored 65 goals in 58 matches for Norway.
Oscar Bobb put Norway ahead in Cardiff, but Daniel James equalized before halftime. Norway defender Torbjørn Heggem was later sent off for fouling James, and Neco Williams scored the winner from the resulting free kick.
Protest disrupts Ireland-Austria match
Protesters calling for Ireland to boycott its upcoming match against Israel on Sunday interrupted Ireland's game against Austria by throwing tennis balls carrying Palestinian flags onto the field during the first half.
A man carrying a Palestinian flag also attempted to enter the pitch before stewards stopped him.
Troy Parrott scored twice, including a fine solo effort, but Austria fought back through Alexander Prass and Michael Gregoritsch in the second half.
In the other Group B3 match, Israel and Kosovo played out a 0-0 draw.
Elsewhere, Liechtenstein held Azerbaijan to a 0-0 draw in Group D2.

item.title: Towards stronger ties with Australia
item.description:
The recent diplomatic engagement with the Australian High Commission could help move our relationship beyond traditional development aid toward a more ambitious, economic-first alliance.
As Bangladesh navigates a critical economic transition, deepening ties with a nation such as Australia across energy security, trade diversification, and technical education is the sort of partnership that could help us with our ambitions for sustainable growth.
At the heart of this evolving relationship is the shared imperative of energy security. As Bangladesh works to power its industrial capacity and meet expanding domestic demand, securing reliable liquefied natural gas (LNG) imports and attracting foreign direct investment in renewable energy, energy exploration, and grid logistics are certainly essential.
Australia, with its vast energy resources, green technology leadership, and expertise in resource management, is a perfect fit to support our transition toward a more resilient and diversified energy matrix.
Equally promising is the focus on human capital development. Expanding pathways for skilled professional migration in engineering, healthcare, and information technology creates valuable opportunities for Bangladeshi talent while helping fill key labour demands in Australia.
Proposals to link Bangladesh’s technical training centres with Australian vocational institutions, alongside efforts to bring offshore university campuses to Dhaka, reflect forward-thinking vision for development. Aligning local skill training with international technical standards is the sort of initiative we need to see to ensure that our youth can learn to compete successfully in the global economy.
Strengthening Bangladesh-Australia cooperation in areas of mutual interest could be crucial for our ongoing economic transformation. This is a partnership that promises long-term stability and mutual prosperity, and we must ensure that we are ready to take this relationship to the next level.

item.title: Getting tougher on public accountability
item.description:
The forced resignation of a sitting lawmaker and the dissolution of local party committees following multiple land grabbing incidents and attempts potentially mark a critical turning point for political governance.
It goes without saying that when public representatives and grassroots operatives become implicated in acts of mob violence, land grabbing, and criminal sabotage, the integrity of the entire political system is compromised.
While organizational dismissals and parliamentary resignations are necessary first steps, and we commend the state for taking swift action, we must go far further to systematically excise bad actors from public life.
Political affiliation in Bangladesh has long functioned as a shield against legal accountability. Local leaders, clout-chasers, and organized muscle have routinely exploited political patronage to seize property, intimidate communities, and subvert laws with complete impunity.
Our law enforcement too is not above criticism; at a time when we have needed them to be proactive and assist with dismantling criminal activities, their passivity has only emboldened criminal behaviour.
What we have is a deep-seated culture of impunity that continues to undermine the rule of law, and it is one that we must eliminate.
Internal party discipline, while commendable, cannot replace state justice. Forcing rogue actors to step down or stripping them of party membership addresses the political optics, but it does not satisfy the demands of the law.
As such, criminal acts must be met with rigorous investigation, transparent prosecution, and severe judicial penalties, regardless of an individual's standing or political ties.
If our country is to break free from the destructive cycles of political hooliganism, we must expect better from our political leaders. The message must be clear: Extortionists and land grabbers have no place here.

item.title: Mithila joins Columbia University, CUNY
item.description:
Actor and development professional Rafiath Rashid Mithila has begun a new chapter in her career after concluding her long association with BRAC.
Mithila has joined Columbia University’s Irving Institute for Clinical and Translational Research as an Associate Research Scientist. She has also taken up a teaching position at the City University of New York (CUNY) as an Adjunct Assistant Professor.
Mithila shared details of her new roles in a social media post.
At Columbia University, she will lead the design and evaluation of the New York-based Early Childhood and Family Hub initiative, focusing on early childhood development, family engagement and community health.
The initiative aims to connect children from birth to 5 years old and their families with resources, services and supportive environments.
Drawing on her experience in international development, Mithila said she hopes to align research objectives with the needs of local communities and contribute to developing effective programmes based on research and evidence.
At CUNY, she will teach Nonprofit Management, focusing on giving students practical insight into the workings and experiences of nonprofit organisations.
Mithila spent two decades with BRAC, including 15 years working in international development with BRAC International.
She expressed gratitude to BRAC for its role in shaping her professional journey and said working within Columbia University’s research environment alongside its researchers would further enrich her experience.
She concluded her post by asking for prayers as she begins the new chapter of her professional journey.

item.title: Tom Cruise unveils new look for ‘Digger’
item.description:
Tom Cruise appears in a dramatically different look in Alejandro G Iñárritu’s upcoming film “Digger”, which is set to release worldwide on October 2 under the Warner Bros banner.
The film will also be released in Bangladesh on the same day.
Known for his action roles and portrayal of Ethan Hunt in the “Mission: Impossible” franchise, Cruise has maintained a recognisable screen persona throughout his more than four-decade career. “Digger”, however, sees him take on a markedly different appearance.
In the film, Cruise appears with grey-white hair, a prominent belly and a heavily lined face. His transformation drew attention following the release of the film’s trailer.
The change involved more than makeup and prosthetics. Cruise said he worked closely with Iñárritu on several aspects of the character, including the costume, makeup, appearance of his teeth, manner of walking, and the rhythm of the music associated with the role.
According to Cruise, a character is shaped by more than dialogue, with visual details also contributing to the storytelling.
The actor also said his more than four decades of experience in the film industry helped him approach the role and move beyond the screen image audiences have long associated with him.

item.title: Case against Maj. (retd.) Akhtaruzzaman for allegedly threating to assault an airport official
item.description:
A case has been filed against Major (Retd.) Akhtaruzzaman over allegations of creating disorder at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in the capital, obstructing government duties, and harassing a security official on duty.

The case was filed on Thursday night at the airport police station by airport security officer Md. Shahriar Alam Sajib. Multiple sections of the Penal Code have been invoked in the case.

Police said the incident occurred over a shortage of luggage carts and trolleys. According to the police, Akhtaruzzaman publicly threatened the airport’s Executive Director, Group Captain SM Ragib Samad, saying, “I’ll grab you and beat you up” and “I’ll grab you by the neck and throw you out.”

Kamrul Hasan Talukdar, officer-in-charge (OC) of the airport police station, told Prothom Alo on Friday that the case includes allegations of obstructing government duties, causing injury, criminal use of force, intentional insult, and intimidation.

Akhtaruzzaman joined Jamaat as an associate member ahead of the 13th national parliamentary election.

According to the case statement, police said that at around 10:45 am yesterday, after passengers disembarked from a Biman Bangladesh Airlines flight (BG-338) arriving from Medina, Saudi Arabia, there was a shortage of trolleys in the area of baggage belt No. 8. The delay in collecting luggage led to frustration and tension among the passengers.

The airport’s Executive Director, Group Captain SM Ragib Samad, went to the scene at the request of Mohammad Kamal Hossain, the Member of Parliament for Dhaka-5, to assess the situation.

Police further said that while he was trying to calm the passengers, Major (Retd.) Akhtaruzzaman approached him aggressively. He openly threatened the executive director, saying, “I’ll grab you and beat you up” and “I’ll grab you by the neck and throw you out.” He also allegedly made extremely obscene remarks about the Minister for Civil Aviation and Tourism.

item.title: Ronaldo's Portugal future in doubt after walkout
item.description:
The international future of Portugal superstar Cristiano Ronaldo hung in the balance after the 41-year-old walked out on the squad after learning that he would not start the game against Denmark on Thursday.

Ronaldo announced late on Wednesday that he had left the team, shortly after a press conference in which coach Jorge Jesus confirmed the five-time Ballon d'Or winner would be left out of his starting line-up for a second consecutive Nations League game.

In his absence, Portugal turned on the style to beat Denmark 4-2.

The former Real Madrid forward had been due to train with his teammates at the Parken Stadium on the eve of the game, but walked out following the announcement by Jesus.

Cristiano Ronaldo: 'This is probably my last year'

"Following the national team coach's press conference, and after having a conversation with the Portuguese Football Federation president, I decided to leave the national team's training camp," Ronaldo wrote on Instagram.

He had already spent the entirety of Sunday's 2-1 Nations League win in Norway on the bench, having captained the side in the 1-0 home victory over Wales last Thursday.

Ronaldo appeared to indicate that the reasons behind Jesus's decision ran deeper, and hinted at a departure from the national team he has graced for more than two decades.

"In due course, I will tell the truth to all the Portuguese people about my reasons for leaving the national team, to which I have always been dedicated," Ronaldo said.

"Now is time to wish good luck to Portugal and to all my team-mates, without exception."

Spanish sports daily Marca said that Jesus and Portuguese federation president Pedro Proenca followed Ronaldo to Copenhagen airport in an attempt to persuade him to stay with the squad, before the player boarded his private jet.

Jesus insisted earlier on Wednesday that there was no rift between him and Ronaldo, although the 72-year-old, who was appointed in July, acknowledged that his captain was disappointed to remain on the bench against Norway.

The news sparked a wave of memes on social media and a furious backlash from Ronaldo's sister, Elma Aveiro.

"They don't deserve to have the best of anything," she said about the Portuguese people on Instagram.

"We are envious, scornful, and ignorant, and we deserve to return to the mediocrity that defined us in the pre-CR7 era of football," she added, using his nickname.

'Players with status'

The game in Oslo was the first time since November 2024 that Ronaldo had not featured for Portugal while not being either injured or suspended.

"There was no incident whatsoever," Jesus, who coached Ronaldo at Saudi club Al-Nassr for a year, insisted after that match.

"Any player -- and I was a player myself... when you spend 20 or 30 minutes warming up and then don't get on... no one is happy about that," Jesus added on Wednesday.

The Portuguese coach also said that he had told Ronaldo before the match that he might bring him on as a substitute.

"Afterwards, as coach, I decided not to bring him on. It's nothing to make a fuss about," Jesus insisted.

After the win on Thursday, Jesus's press conference was dominated by talk of Ronaldo.

"This Portugal team scored four goals and put in a performance which, in my opinion, was of a very high standard," he said.

"Of course, this is more important than anything else that has happened.

"I still think exactly the same way: there are players with status. That much is crystal clear," he added.

"But I'll say it again: the rules are the same for everyone."

There were reports that Portuguese Prime Minister Luis Montenegro had even discussed the issue of Ronaldo's involvement with the coach on Wednesday.

Jesus said earlier in the day that against Denmark he again intended to start AC Milan striker Goncalo Ramos, who scored the winner in Norway.

Regarding Ronaldo, he said: "If I need him, he'll come on. If I don't need him, he won't."

Ronaldo recently announced that this would "probably (be) my last year in football".

He is Portugal's leading goalscorer and most capped player, with 146 goals in 234 appearances.

The former Sporting, Manchester United, Real and Juventus striker made his international debut aged 18 in 2003 and played in the Euro 2004 final when Portugal lost to hosts Greece.

He reached the World Cup semi-finals in 2006 and captained his country to glory at Euro 2016.

Ronaldo and Portugal were eliminated by eventual winners Spain in the last 16 of this year's World Cup.

item.title: bdnews24.com Editor Toufique Imrose Khalidi passes away
item.description:
Toufique Imrose Khalidi, editor-in-chief and publisher of leading online news portal bdnews24.com, has died in London on Friday.
He breathed his last at around 7:00pm (Bangladesh time) on Friday while undergoing treatment at a London hospital, a senior bdnews24.com journalist confirmed to Dhaka Tribune.
According to his colleagues, Khalidi had travelled to London recently for medical treatment. He reportedly became dizzy and collapsed in his hotel room on Thursday night. He was subsequently taken to hospital by ambulance, where doctors declared him dead at around 7:00pm.
“Doctors said he had suffered a brain haemorrhage,” his colleagues said.
Khalidi had served as the publisher and editor-in-chief of bdnews24.com, the online news outlet and news agency he owned, since 2006.
He worked at the BBC in London as a presenter, producer and editor.
In December 2017, Khalidi received the National ICT Award in recognition of his contribution to the development of Digital Bangladesh.

item.title: Altercation at the airport: DB arrests Major (retd) Akhtaruzzaman
item.description:
The Dhaka Metropolitan Police’s Detective Branch (DB) has taken Jamaat-e-Islami leader and former MP Major (retd) Akhtaruzzaman into custody following an altercation at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport.
“DB has taken him into custody,” confirmed DB Additional Commissioner Shafiqul Islam.
Asked about the situation, he said: “DB personnel are at his house. He will accompany them once he finishes his prayers.”
A case has been filed against Jamaat leader Major (retd) Akhteruzzaman over allegations of creating disorder at the airport, obstructing government officials in performing their duties and physically assaulting an on-duty security officer amid a shortage of luggage trolleys.
Airport security officer Md Shahriar Alam Sajib filed the case with Airport Police Station on Friday under several sections of the Penal Code.
According to the case statement, a shortage of luggage trolleys and delays in baggage delivery occurred around 10:40am on October 1 at baggage belt No 8 due to heavy passenger pressure following the arrival of a flight (BG-338) from Madinah.
As tensions among passengers escalated, Airport Executive Director Group Captain SM Ragib Samad went to the spot at the request of Dhaka-5 MP Mohammad Kamal Hossain.
The statement alleges that while the executive director was trying to calm the situation, Akhteruzzaman approached him aggressively and verbally abused him. He allegedly threatened the official, saying, “I will beat you up” and “I will throw you out by the neck.”
He also allegedly made highly offensive remarks about the civil aviation and tourism minister. The situation reportedly worsened when protocol assistants accompanying Akhteruzzaman began recording videos on their mobile phones inside the airport’s restricted Key Point Installation (KPI) area.
When security supervisor Warrant Officer Mohammad Kamal Uddin asked them to stop recording, Akhteruzzaman allegedly became angry, verbally abused him and physically assaulted him.
He is also accused of throwing bottles of holy Zamzam water collected by passengers from trolleys, damaging them, and behaving aggressively towards a representative of Biman Bangladesh Airlines.
The complainant said Akhteruzzaman’s actions obstructed government officials from performing their duties at the sensitive and restricted facility, threatening to disrupt normal airport security and order.
The case was filed under Sections 186, 189, 294, 323, 352, 353, 504 and 506 of the Penal Code on allegations of obstructing public servants, causing hurt, using criminal force, intentional insult and criminal intimidation.
Airport Police Station Officer-in-Charge Kamrul Hasan Talukder confirmed the filing of the case, saying an investigation was underway.
Asked whether Akhteruzzaman would be arrested, the OC said, “We cannot say anything about that at this stage. Since a case has been filed, we will investigate the matter and take necessary legal action.”

item.title: Measles outbreak: Death toll reaches 1,114 as four die in 24 hours
item.description:
Four more children have died from measles and measles-like symptoms in the 24 hours leading up to 8:00am on Friday, raising the overall death toll from the ongoing outbreak to 1,114.
The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) has classified three of the latest casualties as suspected and one as a confirmed measles death.
With the latest figures, the total number of suspected measles deaths has reached 1,012, while the number of confirmed deaths rose to 102, as one new confirmed measles death was reported in the last 24 hours.
The three new suspected fatalities were all recorded in the Dhaka division, specifically within the Dhaka district.
A total of 1,221 suspected measles cases were recorded in the 24 hours till Friday morning, taking the overall suspected case tally to 194,084.
During the same period, 21 new confirmed measles cases were reported, bringing the total number of confirmed infections to 21,623.
Since March 15, 2026, a total of 172,021 suspected measles patients have been hospitalized across the country, of whom 166,933 have recovered and been discharged from hospitals, according to the DGHS 2 oct.png report.

item.title: 7 killed as bus hits autorickshaw in Mymensingh
item.description:
Seven passengers of a CNG-run auto-rickshaw were killed after it was hit by a bus in Mymensingh on Friday afternoon.
The accident occurred around 1:15pm in the East Gandhrapa bypass area of the city.
Four of the deceased have been identified as Minan, 5, son of Kabir Hossain of Dari Hamidpur in Jamalpur Sadar upazila; Rashida Begum, 80, wife of Majum Ali from the same village; Mofazzal Hossain Lebu Mia, 54; and his daughter Marjina, 25.
Efforts are underway to identify the remaining 3 victims.
Confirming the deaths, Mymensingh Kotwali Model police station Officer-in-Charge Shibirul Islam said a Rajib Paribahan bus travelling from Dhaka to Jamalpur collided head-on with a CNG-run auto-rickshaw coming from Muktagachha.
Additional Superintendent of Police Abdullah Al Mamun confirmed that all 7 victims died at the scene. The accident occurred when the Jamalpur-bound bus collided head-on with the auto-rickshaw coming from the opposite direction in the Gandrapa area of Mymensingh Sadar.
The auto-rickshaw was badly damaged in the collision.
Police and Fire Service personnel reached the scene after receiving the information and recovered the bodies. Traffic movement on the road was disrupted after the accident but has since returned to normal.
The Rajib Paribahan bus and the auto-rickshaw involved in the accident are in police custody. Necessary legal procedures, including preparation of the inquest reports of the deceased, are underway.
Traffic movement on the road is currently normal.

item.title: Four remanded over extortion, blank firing in Bangla Motor
item.description:
A Dhaka court on Friday placed four people, including expelled Jubo Dal leader Ferdous Ahmed Saimon, on remand in a case filed over allegedly beating a man and firing blank shots after he refused to pay Tk50,000 in extortion in Bangla Motor area.
Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Israt Jahan passed the remand order after a hearing in the afternoon, granting 4 days’ remand for Saimon, the prime accused, and 3 days each for the other 3 accused.
The other accused sent to remand are Omar, 32, Morshed, 25, and Md Shaon, 25. SI Arif Reza of the prosecution department confirmed the matter.
He said there was no lawyer present for the accused during the remand hearing.
Earlier on Friday, SI Md Nasim, investigation officer of Hatirjheel police station, produced the accused before the court and sought 7 days’ remand for each in the interest of a proper investigation.
According to the case statement, at around 7:15pm on Thursday, October 1, the accused stopped plaintiff Md Sohan in front of a house in the New Eskaton area of Bangla Motors under Hatirjheel police station.
The case statement alleges that prime accused Ferdous Ahmed Saimon demanded Tk50,000 in extortion from him. When Sohan refused to pay, Saimon allegedly pulled out a pistol, pointed it at his chest and attempted to shoot him.
At one point, Saimon allegedly struck Sohan on the head with the butt of the pistol, while the other accused also beat him. The accused left the scene after people nearby approached.
The injured Sohan received first aid at a local pharmacy. Later, while he was travelling for further treatment, his brother-in-law Md Moktar Hossain joined him.
At that time, Saimon and the other accused allegedly arrived at the scene on motorcycles and again attempted to beat Sohan. Moktar Hossain was also allegedly beaten when he tried to intervene, according to the case statement.
The remand application states that Saimon fired 3 blank shots from the pistol at that time. Local people then chased and detained several of the accused.
Saimon was also detained when he attempted to flee. Police from Hatirjheel police station went to the scene after being informed and took them into custody.
Later, victim Md Sohan filed the case with Hatirjheel police station.
The remand application further states that preliminary investigation found the arrested accused to be active members of an organized extortion and criminal group.
The application said the accused needed to be interrogated on remand to identify the identities and whereabouts of others involved, arrest absconding accused and recover other information related to the case.
The police remand application also stated that the arrested accused have several drug cases filed with Hatirjheel and Kalabagan police stations.
